title: P26: sixteen attention heads at fixed residual width
description: P26: increase attention heads from 8 to 16 at fixed residual width 256, four layers and 3210240 parameters, reducing head dimension from 32 to 16. More independent retrieval distributions may represent simultaneous premises and citations better, providing a stronger starting point for the fixed downstream expert-iteration procedure.
hypothesis: Separate attention channels may reduce interference between distinct proof references while preserving unique capacity, unlike the reduced-capacity sharing in failed run 014. Previous depth changes 006/008 and recent optimizer/regularization changes did not improve the incumbent; no earlier registration changes head count. Narrower heads also reduce per-head content and rotary dimensions and change default attention scaling, so this is the standard head-count intervention rather than an isolation of retrieval multiplicity. Too-narrow heads may hurt proof validity. Only downstream three-seed dev-transfer >=7 performance decides keep/discard.
expected_delta: Central prediction +5 to +15 dev-transfer theorems at true length >=7 versus incumbent 012 (exact mean 147.67; stored rounded mean 148), with plausible downside -40. Keep only if the seeds 0,1,2 mean improves. Dense projection FLOPs and total KV-cache elements are unchanged, but twice as many attention distributions and head dimension 16 can reduce fused-kernel efficiency; unmeasured estimate 0-20% lower pretraining throughput and higher sampling latency. Budgets remain 300 seconds pretraining and 1200 seconds total; timeout counts as failure.
